facts: The subject matter of challenge in this appeal is the judgment dated January 16, 1988 rendered by the Designated Court, Rohtak disposing of two cases, being Sessions Case No. 280 of 1986 and Arms Act Case No. 281 of 1986.

On March 20, 1986, three appellants waylaid Attar Chand and Jaggar, who were the Sarpanch and Panch respectively of village Nigana, near a field which was at a distance of 3 Km. from the village abadi.
The three appellants struck Attar Chand and Jaggar with their respective weapons resulting in their instantaneous death.

Satram Dass (P.W.11), brother of Attar Chand, came back home and found that the latter had not returned home till then, he went in his search and ultimately found their dead bodies lying in the field outside the village.
On receipt of the information, Satram Dass Batra went to Kalanaur Police Station at 2.A.M. and lodged a report which reads as under :
The appellants abjured their guilt and contended that they had been falsely implicated in the case owing to enmity.
issues: Whether the prosecution had been able to conclusively prove that the three appellants were responsible for the death of Attar Chand and Jaggar?
petitioner_arguments: The appellants contended that they had been falsely implicated in the case owing to enmity.
court_reasoning: The uncontroverted evidence of SI Mange Ram (P.W.16) and Dr. D.K. Sharma (P.W.1) establishes that both Attar Chand and Jaggar met with homicidal death.
The crucial question that now falls for our determination is whether the prosecution had been able to conclusively prove that the three appellants were responsible for their such death.
holding: The conviction and sentence recorded against the three appellants under Section 302/34 IPC are set aside and they are acquitted.
The appellant Raj Kumar is also acquitted of the charge of unlawful possession of a pistol and a cartridge.
Appellant Ballu and Raj Kumar, who are on bail, are discharged from their respective bail bonds.
Appellant Jagdish, who is on jail, be released forthwith unless wanted in connection with any other case.
